anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After keeps every fact Before kept: A records the HTTP 503 as a failed prerequisite with P1 open and no retry; B treats API success without readback as unconfirmed and leaves P1 open; C and D both keep P1 open on the recheck worker's `open` result and only redraft proposals; E marks the raced write unconfirmed, refuses to reuse 1111111 evidence or repeat the write, and closes P1 only after a fresh Verify claim-check and Review at 2222222. The course-model change lands cleanly (persistent deliver, assess/stop menus, no round charged for body-only work, show evidence as a hint). Two wording points worth tightening so later cases don't drift: A-D all print 'add 6 to each cap' on the deliver row even though no budget was consumed, which reads as an unconditional cumulative extension rather than one tied to a cap obstacle — consider phrasing it as 'resume the retained course (no cap change)' unless usage actually hit the cap; and in E, the record should state explicitly that 'P1 resolved only on new-head Verify claim-check + Review, not on the head refresh' so the fresh-assessment requirement is visible in the text rather than implied by the step list.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After keeps every fact Before kept: A–D each leave the description finding open, report the 503/502/unexpected-body/surviving-contradiction outcome, and forbid a blind re-write; E leaves the old-head operation unconfirmed, re-runs fresh Verify and Review at 2222…, binds new CI evidence to that head, and only then renders final. Two wording risks remain that could move f5 or f2 under a stricter reader. In E, 'The stipulated clean helper results settle the actual-body claims' leans on the simulation stipulation rather than on the helper's own reported closure line; prefer 'the fresh worker reports P1: resolved against the actual new-head body; readiness follows only from that closure line and the matching new-head evidence block', so closure is visibly earned, not asserted. In A and B the open finding sits under 'PR comments:' instead of 'Blockers:', which reads like a drafted comment rather than an unresolved blocker; use the Blockers list (as C and D do) so the open-finding state is unambiguous. Also reconsider the retry rows' 'add 6 to each cap' text: a retry under a retained course with no round charged should not automatically imply a cap extension unless an obstacle has actually exhausted a cap — phrase it as 'resume the retained course (no round charged); cap extension offered only if usage reaches the cap' to stay consistent with the cumulative-cap rule in the Change.
